Package org.krmdemo.plansinstr.equilib

Record Class Sweep

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.krmdemo.plansinstr.equilib.Sweep
Record Components:
thresholdMin - (Tmin) the lowest balance the DDA should keep
thresholdMax - (Tmax) the highest balance the DDA should keep; Tmin ≤ Tmax, and when they are equal, just T: the target balance
nominalMin - (τmin) the smallest sweep In worth making
nominalMax - (τmax) the smallest sweep Out worth making
sweptInMax - (A, available) the balance of the investment account: the most one sweep In can bring back; 0, or at least τmin (a smaller A could never move a whole nominal)
sweptOutMax - (L, limit) the largest single payment into the investment account: above 0 and at least τmax
public record Sweep(long thresholdMin, long thresholdMax, long nominalMin, long nominalMax, long sweptInMax, long sweptOutMax) extends Record
The parameters of a cash sweep, in whole dollars, and the swept amount y for any current balance x of the DDA (the current account).
The swept amount and the sweep status (Zone)
ywhenstatus
Ax < Tmin − ASwept In Partial (A > 0)
Tmin − xTmin − A ≤ x ≤ Tmin − τminSwept In Full (A > 0)
∄ ⏚x ≤ Tmin − τminSwept In Zero (A = 0)
0Tmin − τmin < x < TminIn Nominal Min
0Tmin ≤ x ≤ TmaxIn Range
0Tmax < x < Tmax + τmaxIn Nominal Max
x − TmaxTmax + τmax ≤ x ≤ Tmax + LSwept Out
∄ ⏚x > Tmax + LSwept Out Overflow

The nominals are the smallest transfers worth making: a sweep happens only if it moves at least τ (and more than nothing). So y jumps at Tmin − τmin and at Tmax + τmax, and the point of the jump belongs to the sweep.

The graph, the demo page and the tests name the components by their symbols (in parentheses below); the threshold is written as over the graph: −$8k [$40k ; $60k] +$10k ([$50k] for a target balance, zero nominals left out).
